data.long_meaning: Chaya is derived from the Sanskrit word चया (chaya) which means 'shadow' or 'illusion'. In Hindu mythology, Chaya is the goddess of shadows and is often depicted as a reflection or an echo of reality. She is also associated with creativity and imagination. The name Chaya carries the meaning “Shadow, Illusion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chaya usually hope their child will grow to embody shadow, illusion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
